items.title: 'Young Washington' Director Jon Erwin Breaks Down Film's Use of AI
items.summary: Jon Erwin walks through exactly how his July 4th-weekend historical drama 'Young Washington' used generative AI, scene by scene. The production employed five AI artists plus an AI producer and crew member, with Erwin arguing the tech made the shoot 'safer and more affordable.' The film opened nationwide July 3 and is over-performing at the box office.
items.why: Rare concrete, named-crew breakdown of AI inside a wide-release theatrical feature that is actually succeeding commercially — moves the AI x film story from panels to production reality.
items.notes: Screen Daily's 7/5 box office piece notes 'Young Washington' soaring on opening weekend — usable as supporting context.

items.title: Midjourney Seeks to Reveal Studios' Use of AI in High-Stakes Copyright Battle
items.summary: Midjourney is appealing a magistrate judge's order limiting discovery into how Disney, Universal and Warner Bros. themselves use AI in their shows and movies. The company wants studios' internal AI use on the record as it mounts a fair-use defense in the studios' copyright infringement suit over Superman, Batman and other characters.
items.why: Turns the studios-vs-AI lawsuit inside out: Hollywood's own quiet AI adoption becomes evidence. Directly shapes how openly studios can use generative tools.
items.notes: Engadget ran a follow-up on 2026-07-04 (engadget.com/2207936/midjourney-wants-studios-that-sued-show-court-ai-use/) citing Variety — de-duped, Variety kept as original.

items.title: Next Lab Generation Required Filmmakers to Use Quill and Magnific — Most Embraced VR but Ditched AI
items.summary: The Next Lab Generation program required its six finalist teams to develop pitches using Meta's Quill VR animation software and the Magnific AI upscaler before pitching in Madrid. Cartoon Brew's rundown of the finalist projects finds most teams leaned into VR workflows while quietly dropping the mandated AI tool.
items.why: A counter-narrative data point: when filmmakers are handed AI by mandate, many opt out — grounded in six real projects rather than opinion.
items.notes: JSON-LD datePublished 2026-07-01T10:39:13 (no offset on site; RSS confirms 7/1).

items.title: Hope, AI, and Indie Ambition: The Contradictions That Defined Annecy 2026
items.summary: Cartoon Brew's on-the-ground festival wrap frames Annecy 2026 through its contradictions: official programming embraced AI panels and pipeline talk while the crowd booed AI-made work, and indie ambition surged in parallel. A mood-of-the-industry piece on where animation actually stands with generative tools.
items.why: Synthesizes the animation world's split personality on AI right after the festival — richer than single-incident coverage.
items.notes: OVERLAP RISK: Annecy 2026 AI-short backlash card (Variety takeaways) published 2026-06-30 — this is a different outlet/angle (full wrap), curator should confirm it reads as new.

items.title: Hasbro's TV Contracts Allegedly Ask Child Voice Actors to Sign Rights Away for AI Use
items.summary: The UK-based Agents of Young Performers Association published an open letter alleging Hasbro's contracts ask child voice actors to sign away rights for AI capture, cloning and training, warning that a parent's approval 'should never be a blanket licence' to reuse a child's voice indefinitely.
items.why: Escalates the AI likeness fight to its most sensitive front — minors' voices — with a named studio and organized pushback.
items.notes: Animation Magazine's 6/25 'Child Actor AI Voice Outcry Drags Peppa Pig Into the Mud' covers the same cluster — de-duped, THR kept as primary.

items.title: Hollywood Workers Are Training AI Models as Job Prospects Grow Slim
items.summary: With film and TV work drying up, veteran writers and crew are taking RLHF gigs — rating and refining generative AI outputs for tech companies. THR profiles workers who are effectively polishing the systems that may render their old jobs obsolete.
items.why: The starkest labor irony of the AI era, reported through actual working film professionals rather than union statements.

items.title: Vibe Directing? An AI Startup Run by Ex-Googlers Says Its New Model Can Make It Happen (Exclusive)
items.summary: OpenArt, founded by ex-Googlers, launched 'Director,' a model/tool pitched at both working Hollywood directors and 'everyday Finchers' — promising conversational, iterative control over AI-generated footage, a workflow the company brands 'vibe directing.'
items.why: New tool with a provocative framing: directing itself as a promptable act — a fresh product story beyond the usual video-model horse race.

items.title: 'Apart' Wins Best in Show at SIGGRAPH 2026 Computer Animation Festival
items.summary: SIGGRAPH 2026 (July 19-23, LA) named its Computer Animation Festival winners — 'Apart,' 'Beyond Words' and '18 Months,' with a new Spike Lee short taking a top prize — and unveiled Production Sessions featuring Weta FX, ILM, Pixar and Google DeepMind, including a session on the artist-centered AI-assisted workflow behind 'Dear Upstairs Neighbors.'
items.why: The industry's premier graphics conference putting AI-assisted animation on its main production stage, tied to award-season-credible shorts.
items.notes: AWN byline 'Tuesday, June 23, 2026 at 1:37am' (ET assumed). PARTIAL OVERLAP: 'Dear Upstairs Neighbors' workflow card published 2026-07-02 — this story's core (CAF winners + sessions lineup) is distinct.
